answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement writes. memory_b2 is the closest analogue: regional latency recovered after a clean traffic shift without implying dropped writes. Rollback (memory_b1) remains a live alternative because a release shipped ~30 minutes before the climb, but a release alone does not explain primary-only impact unless it was region-scoped (unverified). Circuit breaking (memory_b4) risks failing customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) historically offloaded report/dashboard reads, not the write path. Capacity add (memory_b3) was pre-peak headroom, not a fix for a region-local write-path fault already at 5x. Verifying b1 and b2 before commit. Flagging settlement-peak failover/consistency risk. Cause is still uncertain (release vs regional infra vs load).
